name: Mucuna pruriens
summary: Mucuna pruriens carries a Grade D rating — preliminary / theoretical evidence. Strongest recorded design is a randomized controlled trial, drawn from 2 recorded studies, 2 in people. Recorded activity centres on neurotransmitter modulation and dopaminergic, which describes mechanism rather than demonstrated benefit. Noted cautions include concurrent MAOI antidepressants due to a documented risk of a severe pressor crisis from combined dopamine and monoamine surge.
description: Mucuna pruriens contains bioactive constituents that support dopaminergic tone, which can plausibly affect mood, motor control, and neurochemical signaling relevant to movement symptoms.
safetyNotes: Contains L-DOPA; avoid casual stacking with dopamine/psychiatric medications.

sources.title: Mucuna pruriens in Parkinson's disease: a double blind clinical and pharmacological study

contraindications: Concurrent MAOI antidepressants due to a documented risk of a severe pressor crisis from combined dopamine and monoamine surge
concurrent levodopa/carbidopa or other Parkinson's medication due to additive dopaminergic effect and unpredictable dosing since mucuna's L-DOPA lacks a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor
psychosis or schizophrenia due to L-DOPA's potential to worsen psychotic symptoms
pregnancy or breastfeeding or use in children due to insufficient safety data
concurrent antipsychotic medication due to opposing dopaminergic mechanisms that may blunt either drug's effect.
